source_refs.note: Exercise 14.2, Question 7: cos(alpha + beta) by the dot product (book p.275), as in Example 8; unit vectors at alpha and -beta. Original figure drawn for the answer.

blocks.explanation:
Yeh trigonometry ki ek identity hai jo hum vectors se saabit karenge, bilkul kitab ki Example 8 ki tarah (wahan \(\cos(\alpha - \beta)\) saabit kiya gaya tha).
Asal khayal: do unit vectors ka dot product do tareeqon se nikalein, ek angle wale formula se aur ek components se; dono barabar honge.
Plan: ek unit vector x-axis se \(\alpha\) upar aur doosra \(\beta\) neeche rakhein, taa ke dono ke beech angle \(\alpha + \beta\) ban jaye.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: do angles \(\alpha\) aur \(\beta\).
Saabit karna hai: \(\cos(\alpha + \beta) = \cos\alpha\cos\beta - \sin\alpha\sin\beta\).
Tareeqa: Unit vectors (length 1) ke liye \(\underline{u}\cdot\underline{v} = |\underline{u}||\underline{v}|\cos\theta = \cos\theta\), aur components se \(\underline{u}\cdot\underline{v} = a_1a_2 + b_1b_2\). Ek hi cheez do tareeqon se nikalein to dono jawab barabar hote hain; yehi barabari identity de deti hai.

Do unit vectors chunein
\(\underline{OA}\) positive x-axis se \(\alpha\) angle upar, aur \(\underline{OB}\) \(\beta\) angle neeche; dono ki length 1 aur dono xy-plane mein.
\[\angle AOB = \alpha + \beta\]
Kyun: Ek angle x-axis se upar ki taraf naapa aur doosra neeche ki taraf, is liye dono vectors ke beech ka poora angle \(\alpha + \beta\) hai. Figure dekhiye. Agar dono upar hote (Example 8) to farq \(\alpha - \beta\) aata.

Components mein likhein
\[\underline{OA} = \cos\alpha\,\underline{i} + \sin\alpha\,\underline{j}\]
\[\underline{OB} = \cos\beta\,\underline{i} - \sin\beta\,\underline{j}\]
Kyun: Length 1 aur angle \(\phi\) wala vector \(\cos\phi\,\underline{i} + \sin\phi\,\underline{j}\) hota hai (unit circle par point \((\cos\phi, \sin\phi)\)). \(OB\) ka angle \(-\beta\) hai, aur \(\cos(-\beta) = \cos\beta\), \(\sin(-\beta) = -\sin\beta\).
Dhyan dein: \(OB\) ke \(\underline{j}\) component ka minus sign hi aakhir mein formula ka minus banta hai; isay bhoolna nahi.

Definition se dot product
\[\underline{OA}\cdot\underline{OB}\]
\[= |\underline{OA}||\underline{OB}|\cos(\alpha + \beta)\]
\[= (1)(1)\cos(\alpha + \beta)\]
\[= \cos(\alpha + \beta)\]
Kyun: Dono unit vectors hain, to lengths 1 aur 1; beech ka angle \(\alpha + \beta\) hai.

Components se dot product
\[\underline{OA}\cdot\underline{OB}\]
\[= \cos\alpha\cos\beta + \sin\alpha(-\sin\beta)\]
\[= \cos\alpha\cos\beta - \sin\alpha\sin\beta\]
Kyun: \(\underline{i}\) wale components ka product \(\cos\alpha\cos\beta\), \(\underline{j}\) wale ka \(\sin\alpha \times (-\sin\beta)\). Jama kiya.

Dono ko barabar rakhein
\[\cos(\alpha + \beta)\]
\[= \cos\alpha\cos\beta - \sin\alpha\sin\beta\]
Kyun: Dono expressions ek hi dot product \(\underline{OA}\cdot\underline{OB}\) hain, is liye barabar hain. Identity saabit ho gayi.

Tasdeeq
\[\alpha = \beta = 45^{\circ}:\ \cos 90^{\circ} = 0\]
\[\tfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\cdot\tfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} - \tfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\cdot\tfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\]
\[= \tfrac{1}{2} - \tfrac{1}{2} = 0 \;\checkmark\]
Kyun: Ek aasaan misaal mein dono taraf zero aaya. Saboot ke baad aisa chhota number test karna achi aadat hai; is se sign ki ghalti foran pakri jati hai. Ek aur baat: agar \(\beta\) ki jagah \(-\beta\) rakh dein to yehi formula Example 8 wala \(\cos(\alpha - \beta) = \cos\alpha\cos\beta + \sin\alpha\sin\beta\) ban jata hai; dono formulas ek hi khayal ke do roop hain, alag alag ratne ki zaroorat nahi.

answer_figure.alt: Unit circle with centre O. Unit vector OA makes angle alpha above the positive x-axis, at A(cos alpha, sin alpha); unit vector OB makes angle beta below it, at B(cos beta, -sin beta). The angle AOB is alpha + beta.
answer_figure.caption: Question 7: \(\underline{OA}\) at angle \(\alpha\) above and \(\underline{OB}\) at angle \(\beta\) below the x-axis, so \(\angle AOB = \alpha + \beta\) (original drawing).
